newsitem.title: USA: Clinton wishes Yeltsin luck for heart operation.
newsitem.headline: Clinton wishes Yeltsin luck for heart operation.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton called Russian leader Boris Yeltsin on Sunday to wish him well on his forthcoming heart surgery, a White House official said.
"It was just a (friendly) call to talk about his pending surgery and to wish him luck," White House spokeswoman Mary Ellen Glynn told reporters with Clinton in Iowa.

The two leaders talked for about 10 minutes before Clinton left Washington on a one-day trip to the nation's heartland where he was to appear with Iowa Democratic Senator Tom Harkin, who is up for re-election.
Glynn said Clinton congratulated Yeltsin, 65, for publicly announcing his forthcoming surgery.
Yeltsin's disclosure 10 days ago that will have bypass surgery was seen in some quarters as an attempt to demonstrate new openness about the Kremlin leader's health.
He suffered two heart attacks last year, and this summer virtually disappeared from public view for weeks. His aides initially said he was exhausted after a long re-election campaign.

An official in Yeltsin's Moscow press office said the Russian leader expressed his gratitude for Clinton's good wishes and for the readiness of U.S. surgeons to take part in pre-operation consultations.

Another Clinton administration official said the two leaders talked about the upcoming meeting between heart specialists who will decide, among other things, the timing of the surgery and the exact procedure.
Two top German cardiologists are expected to join a Russian team of experts to review Yeltsin's case.
Reports have said that U.S. heart specialist Michael DeBakey would participate in the discussions, but DeBakey said last week he had not been approached.
